text: Company Background The Company designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells a variety of related services. The Company's fiscal year is the 52- or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of September. Products iPhone is the Company's line of smartphones based on its iOS operating system. The iPhone line includes iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16, iPhone 15, iPhone 14 and iPhone SE. Mac is the Company's line of personal computers based on its macOS operating system. The Mac line includes laptops MacBook Air and MacBook Pro, as well as desktops iMac, Mac mini, Mac Studio and Mac Pro. iPad is the Company's line of multipurpose tablets based on its iPadOS operating system.

The Mac line includes laptops MacBook Air and MacBook Pro, as well as desktops iMac, Mac mini, Mac Studio and Mac Pro. iPad is the Company's line of multipurpose tablets based on its iPadOS operating system. The iPad line includes iPad Pro, iPad Air, iPad and iPad mini. Wearables includes smartwatches, wireless headphones and spatial computers, including Apple Watch, AirPods, and Apple Vision Pro. Home includes Apple TV and HomePod products. Services The Company's services include Advertising, AppleCare, Cloud Services, Digital Content (App Store, Apple Arcade, Apple Fitness+, Apple Music, Apple News+, Apple TV+), and Payment Services (Apple Card, Apple Pay). Segments The Company manages its business primarily on a geographic basis.

Segments The Company manages its business primarily on a geographic basis. The Company's reportable segments consist of the Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific. Human Capital As of September 28, 2024, the Company had approximately 164,000 full-time equivalent employees. Competition The markets for the Company's products and services are highly competitive, characterized by aggressive price competition and resulting downward pressure on gross margins, frequent introduction of new products and services, and short product life cycles.

Macroeconomic and Industry Risks The Company's operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions. The Company has international operations with sales outside the U.S. representing a majority of total net sales. Adverse macroeconomic conditions, including slow growth or recession, high unemployment, inflation, tighter credit, higher interest rates, and currency fluctuations, can adversely impact consumer confidence and spending. The Company's business can be impacted by political events, trade disputes, geopolitical tensions, conflict, terrorism, natural disasters, and public health issues. Substantially all of the Company's manufacturing is performed by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam.

Substantially all of the Company's manufacturing is performed by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam. Restrictions on international trade, such as tariffs, can materially adversely affect the Company's business and supply chain. Business Risks The Company depends on component and product manufacturing and logistical services provided by outsourcing partners, many located outside the U.S. The Company relies on single-source outsourcing partners in the U.S., Asia and Europe to supply and manufacture many components. The Company's products and services may be affected by design and manufacturing defects. The introduction of new and complex technologies, such as artificial intelligence features, can increase safety risks.

The introduction of new and complex technologies, such as artificial intelligence features, can increase safety risks. Legal and Regulatory Compliance Risks The Company is subject to various claims, legal proceedings and government investigations. The Company faces a significant number of patent claims relating to its cellular-enabled products. Financial Risks The Company's profit margins vary across products, services, geographic segments and distribution channels. The Company generates a significant portion of net sales from a single product (iPhone), and a decline in demand for that product could significantly impact quarterly net sales.

Digital Markets Act Investigations On March 25, 2024, the European Commission announced two formal noncompliance investigations against the Company under the DMA, concerning Article 5(4) (developer communication/promotion rules) and Article 6(3) (default settings, uninstallation, browser choice screen). Fines can be up to 10% of the Company's annual worldwide net sales. Department of Justice Lawsuit On March 21, 2024, the U.S. DOJ and state attorneys general filed a civil antitrust lawsuit against the Company in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey, alleging monopolization in the markets for "performance smartphones" and "smartphones."  Epic Games Epic Games filed a lawsuit alleging violations of antitrust and unfair competition law based on App Store operation.

The court issued an injunction enjoining the Company from prohibiting developers from including external purchasing links. The Company implemented a compliance plan on January 16, 2024, and filed a motion on September 30, 2024 to narrow or vacate the injunction.

General Amazon seeks to be Earth's most customer-centric company, guided by customer obsession, passion for invention, commitment to operational excellence, and long-term thinking. Segments Amazon has organized its operations into three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). Consumers Amazon serves consumers through online and physical stores, focusing on selection, price, and convenience. Amazon manufactures and sells electronic devices including Kindle, Fire tablet, Fire TV, Echo, Ring, Blink, and eero, and offers Amazon Prime membership. Developers and Enterprises Amazon serves developers and enterprises through AWS, offering on-demand technology services including compute, storage, database, analytics, and machine learning. Human Capital As of December 31, 2024, Amazon employed approximately 1,556,000 full-time and part-time employees.

Human Capital As of December 31, 2024, Amazon employed approximately 1,556,000 full-time and part-time employees. Business and Industry Risks Amazon's businesses are rapidly evolving and intensely competitive across physical, e-commerce, and omnichannel retail, e-commerce services, web and infrastructure computing services, electronic devices, digital content, advertising, grocery, healthcare, and logistics. International Operations Amazon's international sales and operations are subject to risks including local economic and political conditions, government regulation, restrictive governmental actions, foreign currency exchange restrictions, and geopolitical events including war and terrorism. China and India specifically regulate Amazon's businesses through licensing requirements that restrict foreign investment and operation. Fraudulent Activities of Sellers Amazon maintains policies to prevent sellers from collecting fraudulent payments or selling unlawful, counterfeit, or stolen goods. Under the A-to-z Guarantee, Amazon may reimburse customers for payments in these situations.

Under the A-to-z Guarantee, Amazon may reimburse customers for payments in these situations. Government Regulation Amazon faces open investigations based on claims that aspects of its operations infringe competition or consumer protection rules, including aspects of Amazon's fulfillment network, Prime, and AWS's cloud services offering. Amazon is litigating matters alleging price fixing, monopolization, and consumer protection claims brought by state attorneys general and the Federal Trade Commission. Tax Risk The Indian tax authority has asserted that tax applies to cloud services fees paid to Amazon in the U.S.; Amazon is contesting this position.

General Microsoft is a technology company committed to making digital technology and artificial intelligence available broadly. Founded in 1975, the company develops and supports software, services, devices, and solutions. Operating Segments Microsoft operates and reports financial performance using three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Productivity and Business Processes primarily comprises Office Commercial (Office 365, Microsoft Teams, Copilot for Microsoft 365), Office Consumer, LinkedIn, and Dynamics business solutions. Intelligent Cloud primarily comprises server products and cloud services, including Azure, SQL Server, Windows Server, and GitHub, plus Enterprise and Partner Services.

Intelligent Cloud primarily comprises server products and cloud services, including Azure, SQL Server, Windows Server, and GitHub, plus Enterprise and Partner Services. More Personal Computing primarily comprises Windows (OEM and Commercial licensing), Devices (Surface, HoloLens), Gaming (Xbox hardware, content, and services including Activision Blizzard, which joined Microsoft in October 2023), and Search and news advertising (Bing, Copilot, Microsoft Edge). Competition Azure faces competition from Amazon, Google, IBM, Oracle, and open source offerings. AI offerings compete with products from Amazon and Google, as well as Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, and other open source offerings, many of which are also current or potential partners. Windows faces competition mainly from Apple and Google.

Windows faces competition mainly from Apple and Google. Xbox and cloud gaming face competition from Amazon, Apple, Meta, and Tencent, and console competition from Nintendo and Sony. Human Capital As of June 30, 2024, Microsoft employed approximately 228,000 people on a full-time basis: 126,000 in the U.S. and 102,000 internationally. Of these, 86,000 were in operations, 81,000 in product research and development, 45,000 in sales and marketing, and 16,000 in general and administration. Research and Development Microsoft currently has a portfolio of over 63,000 U.S. and international patents issued and over 23,000 pending worldwide. Engineering groups include Cloud and AI, Strategic Missions and Technologies, Experiences and Devices, Microsoft AI, Microsoft Security, Technology and Research (including Microsoft Research), LinkedIn, and Gaming.

Engineering groups include Cloud and AI, Strategic Missions and Technologies, Experiences and Devices, Microsoft AI, Microsoft Security, Technology and Research (including Microsoft Research), LinkedIn, and Gaming. Strategic and Competitive Risks Microsoft faces intense competition across all markets. Barriers to entry in many of Microsoft's businesses are low, and the company competes against platform-based ecosystems, vertically-integrated competitors, and open-source alternatives. Microsoft is investing in AI across the entire company and infusing generative AI capabilities into consumer and commercial offerings. Microsoft expects AI technology and services to be a highly competitive and rapidly evolving market, and will bear significant development and operational costs to build AI models, services, platforms, and infrastructure. Cybersecurity, Data Privacy, and Platform Abuse Risks Microsoft has experienced cybersecurity incidents in which threat actors gained unauthorized access to IT systems and data.

Cybersecurity, Data Privacy, and Platform Abuse Risks Microsoft has experienced cybersecurity incidents in which threat actors gained unauthorized access to IT systems and data. As disclosed in a Form 8-K filed January 19, 2024 (amended March 8, 2024), beginning in late November 2023, a nation-state associated threat actor used a password spray attack to compromise a legacy test account and gain access to Microsoft email accounts, and used this to attempt unauthorized access to some source code repositories and internal systems. Issues in the development and use of AI may result in reputational or competitive harm or liability.

Issues in the development and use of AI may result in reputational or competitive harm or liability. AI algorithms or training methodologies may be flawed, datasets may be biased, and content generated by AI systems may be offensive, illegal, inaccurate, or otherwise harmful. Risks may arise from copyright infringement claims related to AI training and output, and new regulations such as the EU AI Act and the U.S. AI Executive Order. Legal, Regulatory, and Litigation Risks The European Commission has designated Windows and LinkedIn as core platform services subject to obligations under the EU Digital Markets Act.
